about: Millbrook Vineyards & Winery was born on a run-down Dutchess County dairy farm that John Dyson bought in 1982. With his brother-in-law David Bova and winemaker John Graziano, he planted European vinifera vines in 1983, on the advice of Finger Lakes pioneer Dr. Konstantin Frank, and released the first wines in 1985. The converted barn on a steep hillside above the village of Millbrook remains the winery today, surrounded by about 30 acres of estate vines.

Tocai Friulano, the signature white of Friuli in northeastern Italy, became Millbrook’s best-known wine. It was chosen for its winter hardiness, since its home in the Alpine foothills is not unlike the cold Hudson Valley, where the vineyard sits at about 800 feet and winters can fall below zero. The winery has traditionally fermented it cool and kept it in stainless steel to preserve its freshness. Millbrook remains one of very few American producers of the grape, and even bottles a single-vineyard version.

Millbrook describes the 2023 as melon, pear, peach and tropical fruit, with succulent acidity and a soft, lingering finish. Its fresh acidity makes it a versatile food wine; Millbrook has long suggested it with antipasti, shellfish and Asian dishes. For a guest who knows Friulano from Italy, it is a chance to taste the grape grown, unusually, in the Hudson Valley.
